briefs.headline: Leeds beat Chelsea 4-1 at Stamford Bridge, their first league win there in 27 years
briefs.summary: Leeds United defeated Chelsea 4-1 at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, their first Premier League win at the ground in 27 years, per ESPN's match report and box score. Emmanuel Emegha put Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute on his full debut, from a Morgan Rogers pass; Noah Okafor equalised three minutes later, Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted a 53rd-minute penalty conceded by Rogers, Okafor scored again in the 58th and Brenden Aaronson added a fourth in stoppage time. Leeds had 21 shots and eight on target to Chelsea's 14 and three; Moises Caicedo went off injured after 20 minutes. Chelsea drop to eighth on 16 points from 11 matches and Leeds climb to sixth on 17. Chelsea are next at Nottingham Forest on Friday at 3 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Williams-Barnett scores on his first start as Tottenham beat Ipswich 2-0
briefs.summary: Tottenham defeated Ipswich 2-0 at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday, per ESPN's match report and box score, with 18-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett scoring in the 15th minute on his first Premier League start, from a Pedro Porro cross, and setting up Dominic Solanke's second in the 51st with a run into the box. Spurs had 18 shots and nine on target to Ipswich's 11 and three, and ESPN's report says it is their first run of three straight home league wins in two years; Savio went off late in his first match back from a seven-week lay-off, and Roberto De Zerbi watched from the stand under a touchline ban. Tottenham are ninth on 15 points from 11 matches and next play at Sunderland on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 9:05 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Houston beats West Virginia 34-31 on a field goal as time expires
briefs.summary: No. 20 Houston defeated West Virginia 34-31 at Milan Puskar Stadium on Saturday before 37,380, Jonathan Dimas kicking a 23-yard field goal as time expired, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story. The Mountaineers led by 10 at 31-21 after Michael Hawkins Jr.'s 10-yard touchdown run early in the third quarter, and did not score again; Makhi Hughes ran for 158 yards and three touchdowns for Houston, the last a 3-yard tying score with 5:25 left, and freshman Keisean Henderson, starting in place of the injured Conner Weigman, threw a 68-yard touchdown pass to Amare Thomas on his first attempt and led the final drive. Cam Cook ran for 131 yards and West Virginia rushed for 329 as a team, but converted 4 of 15 third downs to Houston's 9 of 19. West Virginia is five wins and six losses, two and six in the Big 12, on a third straight defeat, and the AP says it must win at conference leader Utah on Friday at 9 p.m. ET to become bowl eligible.

briefs.headline: Marshall beats Georgia State 28-27 and becomes bowl eligible as a late PAT is missed
briefs.summary: Marshall defeated Georgia State 28-27 at Joan C. Edwards Stadium on Saturday before 24,560, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story. Carlos Del Rio-Wilson threw for 199 yards and three touchdowns, including a 94-yard pass to Chris Culliver in the second quarter, and ran for the go-ahead 2-yard score with 6:30 left after Toby Payne's 5-yard touchdown catch and a two-point pass from receiver Owen Sweeney to Del Rio-Wilson had tied it at 21. Ayden Pereira's 31-yard touchdown pass to Rodshaun Dorsey with two seconds left cut the lead to one, but Samer Layous missed the extra point and the Herd recovered the onside kick. Marshall is six wins and five losses, three and four in the Sun Belt, and finishes the regular season at UL Monroe on Saturday at 1 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Bengals put Burks on injured reserve and rule Risner out for Monday night
briefs.summary: The Bengals placed linebacker Oren Burks on the reserve/injured list with a groin injury on Saturday, the club said in a roster update, and their final Week 11 injury report lists Burks and right guard Dalton Risner (knees) as out for Monday night at Washington. Cornerback Jalen Davis (hamstring) and receiver Andrei Iosivas (thumb) are doubtful; linebacker Swayze Bozeman (forearm), safety Kyle Dugger (quad), guards Dylan Fairchild (oblique) and Brian Parker II (knee) and cornerback Dax Hill, who did not practice Saturday with an illness, are questionable. Joe Burrow carries no game-status designation. Washington lists cornerback Amik Robertson (ankle), running backs Rachaad White (heel) and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) and center Lucas Patrick (concussion) as questionable. Kickoff is 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN.

briefs.headline: Crew beat Inter Miami 3-0 in Game 1 as Tapia scores twice and Schulte makes five saves
briefs.summary: The Columbus Crew defeated Inter Miami 3-0 at Nu Stadium in Miami on Saturday in Game 1 of their best-of-three MLS Cup Playoffs first-round series, per ESPN's match report and the AP game story. Gonzalo Tapia converted a ninth-minute penalty after goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair brought him down, Taha Habroune scored in the 52nd from a Brais Mendez pass and Tapia added the third in the 58th; Patrick Schulte made five saves, two of them on Lionel Messi, and Miami played the second half a man down after Gonzalo Lujan's second yellow card in the 36th. The AP says it is Miami's first shutout loss at the stadium, which opened this year, and that the seventh-seeded Crew came in on a six-match winning run to close the regular season, the league's longest active streak. Game 2 is Friday in Columbus, per the AP; ESPN's schedule endpoint carried no kickoff time this morning.

briefs.headline: Wembanyama scores 50 with 19 rebounds as the Spurs beat the Pelicans 114 to 91
briefs.summary: Victor Wembanyama had 50 points, 19 rebounds, five blocks and four steals as the San Antonio Spurs won 114 to 91 over New Orleans at the Frost Bank Center on Saturday night before 18,708, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story. He scored 32 in the first half, left with 6:29 to play after a three-pointer made it a 26-point lead and finished two short of the career high he set Nov. 4 against Dallas; Stephon Castle added 19 points and six assists, and San Antonio shot 19 of 56 from three. Jeremiah Fears scored 29 and Jordan Poole 25 for the Pelicans, who lost a third straight. Dylan Harper missed a second straight game with a strained left hip. The Spurs have won 14 of 15 and are level with the Lakers atop the Western Conference at 14 wins and three losses; they play at Sacramento on Monday at 10 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Onosato wins the Kyushu basho in a playoff over Wakamotoharu after both finish 13 and 2
briefs.summary: Yokozuna (grand champion) Onosato won the Kyushu basho (tournament) in Fukuoka on Sunday, beating maegashira (rank-and-file) 7 Wakamotoharu by watashikomi (thigh-grabbing push down) in a kettei-sen (championship playoff) after both finished the 15 days at 13 wins and two losses, per the Japan Sumo Association's tournament leaders page and the final-day results carried by Yahoo Japan Sports; Sports Hochi and Sponichi Annex report it as his second straight yusho (championship), his first back-to-back titles since his promotion to yokozuna and his first in Kyushu. In the regular final-day bouts Onosato pushed out yokozuna Hoshoryu, who finished nine and six, and Wakamotoharu beat sekiwake (third-highest rank) Atamifuji by tsukiotoshi (thrust down) after Atamifuji, who had him at the edge, fell first; Atamifuji ends 11 and four with Kinbozan, who forced out maegashira 1 Asanoyama, and Asahakuryu. Ozeki (champion) Aonishiki beat ozeki Kotozakura by kotenage (arm-lock throw) to finish seven and eight, a make-koshi (losing record) all the same, and ozeki Kirishima finished 10 and five. Jiji Press reports the sansho (special prizes) went to Atamifuji for outstanding performance, Tamawashi and Kinbozan for fighting spirit and Wakamotoharu for technique. In juryo (the second division) Wakamotoharu's younger brother Wakatakakage won the title at 14 and one, a win clear of Asahifuji. The JSA's English results and champions pages were still unposted shells at 5:52 a.m. ET; the Hatsu basho opens in January in Tokyo, dates to be confirmed from the JSA schedule.

briefs.headline: Nebraska beats No. 16 Ohio State 31-28 to end a 31-game losing streak against ranked teams
briefs.summary: Nebraska defeated No. 16 Ohio State 31-28 at Memorial Stadium in Lincoln on Saturday, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story, ending what the AP counts as a 31-game losing streak against AP Top 25 opponents; Anthony Colandrea threw three touchdown passes, the last a 26-yarder to Quinn Clark midway through the fourth quarter, and ran for 63 yards and a score, and fans came onto the field after the final kneel-down. The Huskers are seven and four, four and four in the Big Ten; the Buckeyes, also seven and four, have lost three times to unranked teams for the first time since 2011, the AP says, and close at Michigan. In the Big 12, Utah stayed unbeaten at 11 and 0 with a 38 to 17 win at TCU, Texas Tech won 20 to 10 at Baylor to reach 10 and one, BYU won 31 to 29 at Kansas in three overtimes and Oklahoma State won 30 to 27 in overtime at Arizona State on a field goal; elsewhere Rutgers won 25 to 24 at Penn State, Virginia won 41 to 24 over North Carolina and Michigan won 18 to 16 over UCLA in three overtimes.

briefs.headline: Kings end an eight-game skid against Boston as the 76ers and Knicks win late
briefs.summary: Sacramento won 97 to 96 over Boston on Saturday night on Murray's putback with five seconds left, per ESPN's game account, ending an eight-game losing streak and handing the Celtics a third straight loss. Philadelphia won 132 to 129 over Milwaukee to move to 14 wins and three losses atop the East, five straight wins, and Mikal Bridges's buzzer-beating three gave New York a 97 to 96 win over Portland, per ESPN's scoreboard. In the West, Minnesota won 104 to 95 over Memphis to join the Grizzlies and Houston at 12 and five, two games behind San Antonio and the Lakers, and Dallas won 110 to 100 over the Clippers, who have lost three straight.

waters.reading: 88.7 cfs, 1.57 feet at 5:15 a.m., falling on flow against 97.3 cfs and steady on stage against 1.62 feet in the fetcher's 24-hour comparison.
waters.working: The gauge at Dyer reads 88.7 cfs and 1.57 feet, the fetcher's 24-hour comparison 97.3 cfs and 1.62 feet, so the river has dropped under 90 for the first time this week and is still easing; the stage trend reads steady. At 89 cfs and clear it is a long-leader, small-fly problem, the fish on the pocket-water lies and the tailouts rather than the seams, and with another cold night behind it the midday hours fish best once the sun is on the water. A size 18 to 20 midge or a small Blue-winged Olive nymph under a soft indicator on a 12-foot leader through the slower pockets and the tailouts is the pattern, a stonefly nymph as the point fly in the deeper plunge pools where the larger fish hold in cold water, and a sculpin pattern swung tight to the undercut banks in the first and last hour of light. Water this thin and this clear asks for a longer cast, a finer tippet and an approach from downstream.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.57 feet at 5 a.m., falling against 24.88 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 24.6 ft and falling — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Normal pool with ordinary bank access, falling on the fetcher's 24-hour comparison and the lowest the upper gauge has read this week. The wing dams and the riprap are showing rock and the water is clear enough to fish structure rather than the slack behind it: shad are the forage, so a white or shad-pattern swimbait or a lipless crankbait worked down the face of the wing dams and along the riprap is the pattern, slowed down for water that has seen a run of cold nights, with a jig and crawfish trailer on the slack side of the lock wall for the fish holding off the current. A falling pool pulls fish toward the channel end of the wing dams, so the deeper end of each dam is the first cast. The R.C. Byrd tailwater itself is not gauged; this is the pool side.
waters.source: USGS 03201500 (Ohio River at Point Pleasant); config.SPORTSMAN_WATERS

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.48 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 26.24 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.5 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Normal pool, up about a quarter-foot on the fetcher's 24-hour comparison and reading steady, so the lower gauge has firmed while the upper one falls, the pattern of the dam holding pool with less water coming down. Below the dam the pattern is the structure the dam makes: skipjack and shad stack in the current below the gates, and a spoon or a heavy jig worked in the churn, or a live skipjack drifted along the current seams off the lock wall, is the hybrid and catfish setup; the riprap along the Huntington bank fishes a crawfish-colour jig on the slack side where the bank current breaks. Huntington is the downstream bracket, 30-odd river miles below the dam, not the tailwater reading, which the Corps publish and this pipeline cannot fetch.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 11:36 PM (Sat) at 0.1 ft, high 5:50 AM at 4.1 ft, low 12:28 PM at 0.4 ft, high 6:09 PM at 3.4 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: high 4:51 AM at 5.4 ft, low 11:14 AM at 0.1 ft, high 5:06 PM at 4.1 ft, low 11:00 PM at -0.2 ft. Water 62.1F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:36 a.m. Moon waxing gibbous, 94% illuminated, 12.5 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 5:50 AM and 6:09 PM in the sound.
waters.working: The sound's cycle opens with Saturday night's 11:36 PM low at 0.1 feet, tagged (Sat) in the table because it fell before midnight, so Sunday proper carries three events: the 5:50 AM high at 4.1 feet, the highest high of the week, the 12:28 PM low at 0.4 and the 6:09 PM high at 3.4; the next low falls after midnight Monday. The sound lags the surf by 59 minutes on the morning high, 74 on the midday low and 63 on the evening high, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills. The morning ebb drops 3.7 feet from 5:50 to 12:28 and the afternoon flood climbs 3.0 feet to 6:09, and at waxing gibbous, 94% and 12.5 days the moon is about two days short of full, which the file's age puts on Tuesday, so the swings are at their biggest of the fortnight and the inlet current with them. The water at Beaufort read 62.1F at 5:36 a.m., up 0.9 from Saturday's reading. Beach conditions: the NWS active-alerts feed for North Carolina, read at 5:46 a.m., carries High Surf Advisories for the Outer Banks, Hatteras and Ocracoke islands and East Carteret and a Coastal Flood Advisory for Hatteras Island, nothing for Coastal Pender or New Hanover; Saturday's High Surf Advisory for the Topsail beaches ran to 4 a.m. and is off the feed. The Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry report, a monthly, is dated Nov. 1 and is 21 days old, so it is the month's pattern and not this morning's conditions: East Coast Sports reports the piers taking red drum over 32 inches on the north end of the island, smaller reds and the occasional trout in the sound and trout showing in the surf, with trout expected to dominate as the weather cools; Native Son has the 5-to-8-foot seams in the main creeks as the trout target and cut bait the best bet for the reds inside; Speckled Specialist reports live shrimp under a cork as the best approach and 3/16-ounce jig heads with a soft plastic for artificials, trout in 4 to 16 feet with 4 to 8 the most common, black drum to 18 inches over structure; Carolina Flats has topwater for locating trout early, deeper holes later in the day, and soft plastics for reds on the oyster and grass banks; Jolly Roger Pier reports scattered speckled trout, Virginia mullet and spot on the bottom at night and bluefish thick early; Surf City Pier has pompano, black drum and croaker on the bottom. Tied to today's table and a sound in the low 60s: the whole morning ebb is in daylight for once, so red drum's window, the last of the fall, runs roughly 10 a.m. to the 12:28 low, cut menhaden or a finger mullet on a quarter-ounce head a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges where the draining grass dumps bait, or a soft plastic on the oyster and grass banks as the water leaves them. Trout want the first of the afternoon flood once the sun has been on the flats, roughly 1 to 4 p.m., in the 4-to-8-foot creek-channel seams and along the ICWW channel edge on a 3/16-ounce jig head and a small soft plastic worked slowly, or a live shrimp under a popping cork drifted over the oyster bars at the creek mouths; the flooded-grass window for a weedless gold spoon is the hour before the 6:09 high, which falls at dusk, and the evening ebb that follows runs into full dark on the biggest swing of the fortnight. Spot and sea mullet on bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the ICWW channel on the last of the flood, 5 to 6 p.m.; with no surf advisory for the Topsail beaches this morning, bluefish on a metal jig from the beach or the piers in the first light are back on. Flounder are release only.
